functional_semantics.triton: interior avg = 0.25*(top+bottom+left+right), boundary passes the centre through via tl.where(mask_edge, avg, center) (impl_triton.py:38-50).
functional_semantics.cutile: same four-point average and where-select on the interior mask (impl_cutile.py:32-46).
functional_semantics.note: Both reproduce impl_torch.py:7-13 (clone + interior overwrite, centre not in the sum). Generator tensors.py:120-125 gives square grids (cols defaults to rows).

stages.note: Single sweep, single kernel on both sides; boundary handled inside the kernel, not by a host clone.

dependencies.triton: kernel depends only on the output buffer.
dependencies.cutile: kernel depends only on the output buffer.

reduction_scan_sort.note: No reduction; same summation order as the reference (impl_torch.py:8-12).

precision.triton: arithmetic on the loaded dtype, no explicit upcast (impl_triton.py:49-50).
precision.cutile: arithmetic on the gathered dtype, no explicit astype (impl_cutile.py:45-46).
precision.note: Both compute in the native dtype like the reference; contract permits (does not require) an fp32 promotion.

preprocessing.triton: only empty_like inside run; strides passed to the kernel (impl_triton.py:75,84-85).
preprocessing.note: No halo padding, cloning or caching on either side.

intermediate_storage.triton: none; five masked loads per tile are register resident (impl_triton.py:40-47).

hardware_dispatch.note: Neighbour access (masked pointer loads vs gathers with padding_value 0.0) and tail handling (masked store vs clipped store) are mapping choices. cuTile's mask_center (impl_cutile.py:36) is dead code.

fq_boundary.note: Counts one compulsory read of IN and one write of OUT (plus 3 adds + 1 multiply per element), hard-coding cols == rows, which holds for every case (config sweeps rows only; generator defaults cols to rows). Both implementations issue five loads/gathers per element (the re-reads are cache hits in the minimal-traffic model). Nothing is untimed or prepacked; the output allocation is inside run().
